name: @projexlight/api-gateway
summary: The single front door for ProjexCloud — Fastify HTTP/HTTPS service that composes ~30 SDKs (vault, audit, identity, pool-router, meter, secrets, tenant, consent, policy, rebac, api-keys, projection, media, notification, payment, workflow, billing, webhook, etc.) into one tenant-scoped surface. Wires JWT auth, pool routing, meter gates, and the public REST endpoints every customer + admin SDK talks to.

events.name: api-gateway.boot.completed.v1
events.description: Gateway started; carries SDK boot order + migration status.

events.name: api-gateway.request.served.v1
events.description: Per-request envelope (sampled); feeds sdk-trace + cost attribution.

events.name: api-gateway.failover.engaged.v1
events.description: Active-active failover engaged for this region.

hooks.name: startGateway
hooks.description: Boot the gateway — runs SDK migrations in order, registers route handlers, starts background workers, opens listeners.

hooks.name: registerPlugin
hooks.description: Register an additional Fastify plugin (rare; for tenant-customized routes).

hooks.name: drainAndShutdown
hooks.description: Graceful drain: stop accepting new requests, finish in-flight, flush meter + audit buffers, exit.

scenarios.title: Boot wires every composed SDK in dependency order
scenarios.when_to_use: Process startup. Foundation SDKs initialize first (vault, secrets, audit), then domain SDKs (tenant, identity), then operational (meter, billing), then verticals.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Service listens; emits .boot.completed.v1 with per-SDK boot status. Health endpoint reports green.

scenarios.title: Per-request lifecycle: auth → route → meter → response
scenarios.when_to_use: Universal — every inbound HTTP request goes through this flow.
scenarios.example_code:
// implicit pipeline: jwt verify → tenant scope → policy check → meter.check → handler → meter.report → audit emit → response
// gateway exports the middleware stack so other services can re-use it
scenarios.expected_outcome: Request served with trace span. Sampled into .request.served.v1 for cost attribution + observability.

scenarios.title: Rolling deploy → graceful drain
scenarios.when_to_use: Kubernetes preStop hook calls drainAndShutdown — gateway stops accepting new requests, finishes in-flight within GRACEFUL_DRAIN_SEC, flushes buffers, exits 0.
scenarios.example_code:
import { drainAndShutdown } from '@projexlight/api-gateway';
process.on('SIGTERM', () => drainAndShutdown({ timeout_sec: 30 }));
scenarios.expected_outcome: Zero-downtime deploy. Trace shows no abandoned requests.

scenarios.title: Active-active failover when home region degrades
scenarios.when_to_use: Tier-G+ deployment — region health drops; pool-router flips traffic to the partner region; gateway emits .failover.engaged.v1 for the audit chain.
scenarios.example_code:
// driven by sdk-pool-router health probes;
// gateway role is to emit the event + adjust its readiness probe response.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Traffic shifts within seconds. Failover event audited. SLO clock continues against the partner region until recovery.

scenarios.title: meter.hardcap.denied.v1 → 429 response with policy detail
scenarios.when_to_use: Tenant exceeded a hard cap; gateway translates the event into a structured 429 with retry-after + the violated SKU.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Caller sees 429 with details. Cache invalidates on the next billing-cycle reset.

compliance_posture.notes: Single entry point means every request has a uniform audit chain + meter gate. Failover events satisfy SOC2-CC7.1 availability evidence. Graceful drain ensures no audit-row loss during deploys.
